extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent applicants/attorneys (patent practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and examiner guidance for execution, content, and correction of oaths or declarations and inventor-identifying information in U.S. patent applications (names, citizenship, residence, mailing address, signatures, joint inventorship, and related procedural steps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath or declaration must comply with 37 CFR 1.67(a) and identify application
rubrics_metrics.description: A new oath or declaration in compliance with 37 CFR 1.67(a) identifying this application by application number and filing date is required when the oath or declaration is defective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 6.05 (and one or more of form paragraphs 6.05.01–6.05.20) to notify applicant; if none of the specific form paragraphs apply, give an appropriate explanation of the defect immediately following paragraph 6.05. See MPEP §§ 602.01 and 602.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship of each inventor must be stated
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath or declaration must identify the citizenship of each inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If citizenship is omitted, use form paragraph 6.05.03 (preceded by form paragraph 6.05). OPAP may indicate omissions on a 'Notice of Informal Application.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Residence (city and state or foreign country) required
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s place of residence — the city and either state or foreign country — is required to be included in the oath or declaration in a nonprovisional application for compliance with 37 CFR 1.63 unless included in an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applicants in U.S. Armed Services, a statement to that effect is sufficient. For provisionals, residence must be included on the cover sheet unless in an application data sheet. If omitted, OPAP normally indicates this on a 'Notice of Informal Application' requiring submission within a set period. Use form paragraphs 6.05 and 6.05.02 when residence is omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing (post office) address required and must be applicant's address
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant’s mailing or post office address is required to be supplied on the oath or declaration, if not stated in an application data sheet. Mailing address means the address at which the applicant customarily receives mail; home or business address is acceptable; include ZIP code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address of attorney with instruction to send communications to applicant in care of the attorney is not sufficient. Oaths filed prior to certain dates have special handling; see rules for December 1, 1997 and November 29, 2000. If omitted, use form paragraph 6.05.19 (Mailing Address Omitted) and OPAP will notify applicant as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full given name requirement for each inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.63(a)(2) requires each inventor be identified by full name, including the family name and at least one given name without abbreviation together with any other given name or initial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 6.05 and 6.05.18 may be used to notify applicant if the full given name is not adequately stated. Special rules: a full given name may be a singular letter (e.g., 'J. Doe') if that's the given name — applicant should point that out in the oath. Typewritten middle names may differ from signature; typewritten name controls for the application. Corrections of names (other than typographical/transliteration) generally require a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 and appropriate fee; after issue fee payment, petitions to change names are not grantable and other remedial steps are described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/declaration must be executed by all actual inventors (with limited exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath or declaration (§ 1.63), including any supplemental oath or declaration (§ 1.67), must be made by all of the actual inventors except as provided in §§ 1.42, 1.43, 1.47, or § 1.67.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the person signing is not the inventor (per §§ 1.42, 1.43, 1.47, or 1.67), the oath must state the relationship of the person to the inventor and, upon information and belief, the facts which the inventor is required to state. If the signer is the legal representative of a deceased inventor, the oath must state that status and provide the representative's citizenship, residence, and mailing address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application filed must be the application executed by the applicant (no post-execution alterations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application filed must be the application executed by the applicant; it is improper for anyone, including counsel, to alter, rewrite, or partly fill in any part of the application, including the oath or declaration, after execution of the oath or declaration by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interlineations, erasures, cancellations or other alterations must be made before signing the accompanying oath/declaration and should be dated and initialed by the applicant on the same sheet (37 CFR 1.52(c)(1)). Alterations made after signing require a supplemental oath/declaration under § 1.67 and possibly a substitute specification (§ 1.125). Non-initialed and/or non-dated alterations can be objected to using form paragraph 6.02.01; the Office will require a new oath/declaration if alterations are not initialed and dated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initialing and dating of alterations required
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interlineation, erasure, cancellation or other alteration of the application papers must be made before signing and should be dated and initialed or signed by the applicant on the same sheet of paper; if not, the examiner may require a new oath/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 6.02.01 Non-Initialed and/or Non-Dated Alterations in Application Papers to object. If alterations are made after signing, follow rules for supplemental oath (§ 1.67) or substitute specification (§ 1.125).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Filing System (EFS) signature and scanned declarations allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed through the Electronic Filing System must also contain an oath or declaration personally signed by the inventor; EFS may include scanned images of a declaration executed by the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reformatting of an application when preparing EFS is not an 'alteration' requiring a substitute oath/declaration. It is acceptable to print and have the inventor review and sign a paper copy and then submit a scanned copy with the EFS submission. Reformatting does not require a supplemental oath if done before signing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each oath/declaration must list all inventors; separate individual declarations required
rubrics_metrics.description: While each inventor need not execute the same oath or declaration, each oath or declaration executed by an inventor must contain a complete listing of all inventors so as to clearly indicate what each inventor believes to be the appropriate inventive entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where individual declarations are executed, they must be submitted as individual declarations rather than combined into one declaration (i.e., do not combine signature pages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign on behalf of an inventor (joint inventors, legal representatives, parties with proprietary interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 116 allows joint inventors to sign on behalf of an inventor who cannot be reached or refuses to join. 35 U.S.C. 117 allows a legal representative of a deceased or incapacitated inventor to sign. 35 U.S.C. 118 allows a party with proprietary interest in the invention to sign if the inventor cannot be reached or refuses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An attorney may not sign on behalf of the inventor unless the attorney has a proprietary interest. Case law (e.g., Staeger v. Commissioner, In re Striker) supports that an oath/declaration signed by an attorney without proprietary interest is defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of inventor names controls patent heading
rubrics_metrics.description: The order of names of joint patentees in the heading of the patent is taken from the order in which the typewritten names appear in the original oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully select the preferred order before filing since requests for subsequent shifting require a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 and are not allowed after payment of the issue fee. If separate oaths/declarations are filed, the order is taken from the order in which they appear unless a different order is requested at filing. Applicants are encouraged to submit an application data sheet showing desired order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: When a request to add or delete inventors under 37 CFR 1.48 is granted, the change should be noted in red ink in the left margin of the original oath or declaration (paper files) and appropriate database and file-wrapper corrections made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For IFW/09/ or later series applications, TC technical support or OPAP will update PALM database and print new bib-data sheet. Include an 'Application Division Data Base Routing Slip' brief explanation when forwarding to OPAP. Applicants must correct inventorship pursuant to 37 CFR 1.48 when amendments to claims change inventorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint inventorship contribution standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventors may apply for a patent jointly even though they did not physically work together or at the same time, each did not make the same type or amount of contribution, or each did not make a contribution to the subject matter of every claim of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each named inventor must have made a contribution, individually or jointly, to the subject matter of at least one claim of a nonprovisional application (37 CFR 1.45(c)). For provisional applications (which may be filed without claims), each named inventor must have made a contribution to the subject matter disclosed in the provisional. Examiner should assume common ownership unless evidence to the contrary and should not inquire about inventors/dates until necessary to examine the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction/divisional and inventorship implications
rubrics_metrics.description: If a joint application includes more than one independent and distinct invention, restriction may be required and a divisional application complying with 35 U.S.C. 120 may be needed; this may result in changes to inventorship if the elected invention was not the invention of all originally named inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different claims of an application or patent may have different invention dates; when necessary the Office or a court may inquire of the applicant concerning inventors and invention dates for various claims. Examiner should remind applicants of necessity to correct inventorship under 37 CFR 1.48 if claims are amended so that named inventors are no longer inventors of remaining claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose lack of common ownership and relevant invention dates
rubrics_metrics.description: If inventors of subject matter were not commonly owned at the time of the later invention and file a joint application, applicants have an obligation pursuant to 37 CFR 1.56 to point out inventor and invention dates of each claim and the lack of common ownership so the examiner may consider applicability of 35 U.S.C. 102/103 provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should assume applicants are complying with their duty of disclosure unless evidence to the contrary; failure to disclose may affect rejections under 102(f)/103 or other statutory grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-written signatures and use of titles
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant is unable to write, his or her mark as affixed to the oath or declaration must be attested to by a witness; in the case of the oath, the notary's signature to the jurat is sufficient to authenticate the mark. It is permissible to use a title (e.g., 'Dr.') with the signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles will not appear in the printed patent. Signatures in non-English characters are accepted; there is no required particular manner of signature (see MPEP § 605.04(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Name corrections and timing relative to issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to an inventor's name after filing require a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 and an appropriate petition fee; applicants are encouraged to file an application data sheet showing the new name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition to change the inventor's name cannot be granted if filed after payment of the issue fee. If the error is discovered after payment of the issue fee, either (A) withdraw from issue under 37 CFR 1.313(c)(2) and request correction with an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114, or (B) file a certificate of correction after the patent issues requesting correction.
